note: Section 4.6 counts Configure-Naks sent without sending a Configure-Ack. TestConfiguredLCPMaxFailure and TestRFC1661ClientMaxFailureConvertsFurtherNak each exercise configured limits of two and five, require Naks through the limit, and require the next reply to be a Reject carrying the original unacceptable MRU bytes. The server test and TestRFC1661ClientMaxFailureAckRenewsBudget separately require a successful Ack to renew the budget. Both transport configurations reach the shared server counter; the client schema and Dial snapshot reach negotiateLCP's counter. These assertions distinguish a fixed limit, premature rejection, substituted suggestion bytes and a missing Ack reset. This judgment covers the implemented LCP Configure-Nak senders; it makes no claim about absent IPv6CP counter configuration.
